content.text: The candidate has bp_distance 40. The dominant problem is a spurious long-range helix between linkers (positions 61-74 ↔ 260-270) that outcompetes the small hairpins and multiloop closing pairs. Let me hand-build a clean sequence: GC stems, stable GAAA-style loops, A-rich linkers to suppress spurious pairing.

input.command:
cat > /tmp/build_seq.py << 'PYEOF'
target = "...((....))....(((((((((.........)))))))))....((((.....)))).....(((....)))...(((((.......)))))....(((...((....)).....(((....)))....((((((.......))))))....(((....))).....((((((....(((.......)))..(((........)))...(((((......)))))...((((.....))))..)))))).........((....)).....((....))......(((((..........)))))......)))"
n = len(target)
assert n == 316, n

# parse pairs
stack = []
pairs = {}
for i,c in enumerate(target):
    if c=='(':
        stack.append(i)
    elif c==')':
        j = stack.pop()
        pairs[(j,i)] = True

seq = ['A']*n  # default unpaired = A

# group pairs into stems (consecutive)
pair_list = sorted(pairs.keys())  # by i
# assign G/C alternating per stem
# build stems: consecutive pairs where (i,j),(i+1,j-1)
stems = []
used = set()
for (i,j) in pair_list:
    if (i,j) in used:
        continue
    # extend
    stem = [(i,j)]
    used.add((i,j))
    a,b = i,j
    while (a+1,b-1) in pairs and (a+1,b-1) not in used:
        a+=1; b-=1
        stem.append((a,b))
        used.add((a,b))
    stems.append(stem)

# assign each stem: 5' = GCGC..., 3' = matching
for stem in stems:
    for k,(i,j) in enumerate(stem):
        if k%2==0:
            seq[i]='G'; seq[j]='C'
        else:
            seq[i]='C'; seq[j]='G'

# find hairpin loops (closing pair where inner region is unpaired)
hairpins = []
for stem in stems:
    # innermost pair = last in stem (smallest i among... actually stem is ordered outer->inner by construction)
    (ic, jc) = stem[-1]  # innermost closing pair
    loop_start = ic+1
    loop_end = jc-1
    # check all unpaired in loop
    looplen = loop_end - loop_start + 1
    if all(target[k]=='.' for k in range(loop_start, loop_end+1)):
        hairpins.append((ic,jc,loop_start,loop_end,looplen))

# assign loops
for (ic,jc,ls,le,ll) in hairpins:
    if ll == 4:
        loop = "GAAA"
    elif ll == 5:
        loop = "GAAAA"
    elif ll == 6:
        loop = "GAAAAA"
    elif ll == 7:
        loop = "GAAAAAA"
    elif ll == 8:
        loop = "GAAAAAAA"
    elif ll == 9:
        loop = "GAAAAAAAA"
    elif ll == 10:
        loop = "AAAAAAAAAA"
    else:
        loop = "A"*ll
    for k,ch in enumerate(loop):
        seq[ls+k] = ch

# multiloop closing pairs are single-pair stems (length 1) - already assigned G-C
# verify all paired positions are G/C
result = ''.join(seq)
print(result)
print("LEN", len(result))

# sanity: check complementarity of all pairs
comp = {'G':'C','C':'G','A':'U','U':'A'}
ok = True
for (i,j) in pairs:
    if comp[seq[i]] != seq[j]:
        ok = False
        print("MISMATCH", i, j, seq[i], seq[j])
print("PAIRS_OK", ok)
print("NSTEMS", len(stems))
print("NHAIRPINS", len(hairpins))
PYEOF
